text: Listen to an announcement in a biology class.
script: W: Good morning, everyone. This is an announcement for students in Biology one oh one.
W: Tomorrow's lab will not take place in Room two twelve. The room is being painted this week, so we are moving to Room three oh four, on the third floor of the Science Building.
W: The lab will still start at ten o'clock, and the topic stays the same. You will study plant cells under the microscope.
W: Please bring your lab notebook and wear closed shoes. If you cannot find the new room, ask at the front desk of the Science Building.

stem: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To move the lab to another room
To say that tomorrow's biology lab is cancelled this week
To explain how to use a microscope correctly
To ask students to help paint a classroom
explanation: The speaker says 'we are moving to Room three oh four' because Room two twelve is being painted. The lab is not cancelled; it 'will still start at ten o'clock'. Painting is the reason for the move, not a task for students.

stem: What should students bring to the lab?
options: A plant from their own home garden
A microscope
Their lab notebook
A painting apron and old clothes
explanation: The speaker says 'Please bring your lab notebook and wear closed shoes.' The microscopes are used in the lab, and plants are only the topic, so students do not bring them.

text: Listen to an announcement about library hours.
script: M: Attention, library visitors. Here are some changes to our opening hours for next week.

M: Because of the holiday on Monday, the library will be closed all day. On Tuesday and Wednesday, we will open at nine in the morning and close at six in the evening, which is two hours earlier than usual.
M: From Thursday, we return to normal hours, and we stay open until eight every night so you can study for exams.
M: If you need to return a book while we are closed, please use the blue box outside the main door. Thank you, and have a good week.

stem: What is the announcement mostly about?
options: New rules for borrowing library books
A temporary change in opening hours
A new quiet study room for exams
A holiday event at the library
explanation: The speaker begins with 'changes to our opening hours for next week' and then lists the days. Borrowing rules and events are never discussed; the holiday only explains why Monday is closed.

stem: What can students do if they need to return a book while the library is closed?
options: Leave it with the librarian on Monday morning
Mail it to the library office
Wait until Thursday at eight in the evening
Put it in the box outside the main door
explanation: The speaker says 'please use the blue box outside the main door'. Thursday is only when normal hours begin again, and the speaker never mentions mailing a book.

text: Listen to a voicemail message from a dentist's office.
script: W: Hello, this message is for Priya Nair. I'm calling from Bright Smile Dental Clinic.
W: You have an appointment with Dr. Evans tomorrow at two thirty. Unfortunately, Dr. Evans has to attend a meeting, so we need to move your visit to four o'clock on the same day.
W: If four o'clock is not good for you, please call us back and we will find another time this week.
W: Our number is on your appointment card, and the front desk is open from eight to five. Please remember to arrive ten minutes early to fill out a short form. Thank you, and goodbye.

stem: Why is the woman calling Priya?
options: To remind her to pay an unpaid bill
To say her teeth need more treatment
To change the time of her appointment
To cancel her visit completely this week
explanation: The caller says 'we need to move your visit to four o'clock'. The visit is moved, not cancelled, and no bill or treatment is mentioned.

stem: What should Priya do if the new time does not suit her?
options: Arrive ten minutes early anyway to fill a form
Call the clinic to arrange another time
Visit Dr. Evans at two thirty as planned
Send a message on the clinic's website
explanation: The caller says 'please call us back and we will find another time this week'. Two thirty is the old time, and arriving early is advice for the appointment itself.

text: Listen to an announcement about a campus event.
script: M: Hello, students. I'm happy to tell you about this Friday's International Food Festival.
M: The festival will be held on the main lawn from noon until five o'clock. More than twenty student clubs will serve dishes from their home countries, and each plate costs only two dollars.
M: There will also be music and dancing on the small stage near the bookstore.

M: If it rains, the event will move indoors to the Student Center. And if you would like to help set up tables on Friday morning, please meet Ms. Alvarez at the Student Center at nine. Come hungry, and bring your friends.

stem: What is the speaker mainly doing?
options: Selling tickets for a student concert
Asking clubs to cook for a contest
Giving directions to the campus bookstore
Inviting students to a food festival
explanation: The speaker opens with 'I'm happy to tell you about this Friday's International Food Festival' and gives details to attract students. There is music, but no concert tickets are sold, and the bookstore is only a landmark.

stem: Where will the festival take place if the weather is bad?
options: In the Student Center
In the campus bookstore building
On the small stage by the bookstore
In a club room
explanation: The speaker says 'If it rains, the event will move indoors to the Student Center.' The small stage is near the bookstore, but that is the outdoor location of the music.

text: Listen to an announcement in a residence hall.
script: W: Hello, residents of Maple Hall. This is Dana, your resident advisor, with a few reminders.
W: Starting next week, quiet hours begin at ten o'clock on weeknights, not eleven. Many residents have early classes, and we want everyone to sleep well.
W: Please keep music low and use headphones after ten. Guests are welcome, but they must leave the building by midnight.
W: Also, the laundry room on the first floor will be closed for repairs on Saturday. You can use the laundry room in Oak Hall instead. If you have any questions, my door is room one fourteen.

stem: What is the main change that Dana announces?
options: Guests may stay all night
Quiet hours will start an hour earlier
The residence hall will close for repairs
Music is not allowed in the building
explanation: Dana says quiet hours will begin 'at ten o'clock on weeknights, not eleven'. Music is allowed at a low volume, and only the laundry room, not the hall, is closed.

stem: Where can residents do their laundry on Saturday?
options: In the first floor laundry room
In Dana's room
In Oak Hall
In Maple Hall's basement
explanation: The first floor laundry room is closed for repairs, so Dana says 'You can use the laundry room in Oak Hall instead.' Room one fourteen is where Dana lives, not a laundry room.

text: Listen to an announcement about a final exam.
script: M: Good afternoon. This message is for all students taking the Economics one fifty final exam.
M: The exam will be on Thursday at nine in the morning, as planned. However, because so many students are taking it, we are using two rooms instead of one.
M: If your last name begins with A through L, go to Hall B in the Business Building. If your last name begins with M through Z, go to Room one oh five in the Arts Building.
M: Bring your student card and two pencils. Calculators are allowed, but phones must stay in your bag. Please arrive twenty minutes early. Good luck, everyone.

stem: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To change the date of the exam
To say that calculators are no longer allowed
To explain how to prepare for the exam
To tell students where to take the exam
explanation: The speaker says the exam uses two rooms and tells students where to go by last name. The date stays 'Thursday at nine', and calculators are allowed.

stem: Where should a student named Kim Soo-ah go?
options: Hall B in the Business Building
Room one oh five in the Arts Building
The front office
Any room she likes
explanation: Kim's last name begins with K, which is between A and L, so she goes to 'Hall B in the Business Building'. The Arts Building room is for last names M through Z.

text: Listen to an announcement about a field trip.
script: W: Hello, geology students. I have important news about next Saturday's field trip to Red Rock Canyon.
W: The bus will leave from the parking lot behind the gym at seven thirty, not eight o'clock as we first planned. The road to the canyon is long, and we want to avoid the traffic.
W: Please wear strong walking shoes and bring a hat, sunscreen, and at least two bottles of water. There are no shops in the canyon.
W: Lunch will be provided by the department. If you have any food allergies, email Professor Hall before Wednesday. Thank you.

stem: What has changed about the field trip?
options: The place that students will visit
The cost of the bus ticket
The time the bus will leave
The food that students must bring
explanation: The speaker says the bus will leave 'at seven thirty, not eight o'clock as we first planned'. The destination is still Red Rock Canyon, and the department provides lunch.

stem: What must students with food allergies do?
options: Bring their own lunch to the canyon
Buy food at a shop on the way
Skip the trip on Saturday
Send an email to Professor Hall
explanation: The speaker says 'email Professor Hall before Wednesday'. There are no shops in the canyon, and nothing suggests students with allergies should stay home.

text: Listen to an announcement at a club meeting.
script: M: Welcome, everyone, and thanks for coming to the first meeting of the Hiking Club this semester.
M: I'm Lucas, your club president. We have forty new members this year, which is wonderful.
M: Our first trip will be on Sunday, the fourteenth. We'll walk the lake trail, which takes about three hours and is good for beginners.
M: To join the trip, please sign the list by the door and pay five dollars for transport. Next, let's hear from Aisha, our treasurer, about the club's budget. After that, we'll have tea and cookies.

stem: What is Lucas mainly doing in the announcement?
options: Welcoming members and describing a trip
Asking all members to pay a yearly club fee
Choosing a new club president
Teaching beginners how to hike
explanation: Lucas welcomes the group and then explains the first trip on the lake trail. He is already the president, and the five dollars is for transport, not a yearly fee.

stem: What must students do to join the first trip?
options: Speak to Aisha during the tea break
Bring their own lunch and tea
Walk three hours to the lake
Sign the list and pay five dollars
explanation: Lucas says 'please sign the list by the door and pay five dollars for transport'. Aisha will talk about the budget, which is a different task.

text: Listen to an announcement in a store.
script: W: Attention, shoppers. Welcome to Greenfield Market, and thank you for shopping with us today.
W: For the next two hours, all fresh fruit and vegetables in aisle three are fifteen percent off. This includes apples, tomatoes, and our new local strawberries.
W: Please note that the bakery will close at six o'clock tonight, one hour earlier than usual, because of a staff meeting.
W: If you would like fresh bread for dinner, we suggest you visit the bakery soon. Finally, a reminder that shopping carts must be returned to the front of the store. Thank you.

stem: What is on sale at the moment?
options: Fresh bread
Fruit and vegetables
Shopping carts
Staff meeting tickets
explanation: The speaker says fresh fruit and vegetables in aisle three are 'fifteen percent off' for two hours. The bread is not on sale; the speaker only warns that the bakery closes early.

stem: Why will the bakery close early today?
options: Because it has sold all its bread
Because the staff have a meeting
Because the oven is broken
Because of a holiday sale
explanation: The speaker says the bakery closes at six 'because of a staff meeting'. No other reason is given.

text: Listen to an announcement about a bus service.
script: M: Good morning, riders. This is a service update from University Transit.
M: Starting Monday, Bus Route Five will take a different road because of construction on Park Street. The bus will no longer stop at the Park Street stop or at the post office.
M: Instead, please use the new stop on Garden Avenue, next to the science library. It is about a five minute walk from the old post office stop.
M: The bus will run every fifteen minutes, as usual. You can see a map of the new route on our website or at any bus stop. We are sorry for the trouble and thank you for your patience.

stem: Why will Route Five change?
options: There are fewer riders than before
The buses will run less often
The drivers are changing their routes
Work is being done on a street
explanation: The speaker says the route changes 'because of construction on Park Street'. The bus will still run every fifteen minutes, so it is not less frequent.

stem: Where should riders go to catch the bus instead of the Park Street stop?
options: Garden Avenue
The post office
The science building lobby
The website
explanation: The speaker says 'please use the new stop on Garden Avenue, next to the science library'. The post office stop will no longer be used.

text: Listen to an announcement in a chemistry class.
script: W: Before we finish today, I have two reminders about our chemistry class.
W: First, the homework due on Friday has been moved to the following Monday. Many of you told me the problems were harder than expected, and I agree they need more time.
W: Second, we will have a short quiz at the start of next Tuesday's class. It will cover only the chapter on acids and bases, which we finished this week.
W: The quiz will take ten minutes. If you need help, I'll be in my office on Thursday afternoon from one to three. Please enjoy your weekend.

stem: Why is the homework deadline being changed?
options: The professor will be away from campus on Friday
The students need more time for hard problems
The quiz has been moved forward to Friday
The chapter was not finished
explanation: The speaker says students found the problems 'harder than expected' and need 'more time'. The chapter was finished this week, and the quiz is on Tuesday.

stem: What will the quiz cover?
options: All the homework problems
The whole semester so far
Only acids and bases
The professor's office hours
explanation: The speaker says the quiz 'will cover only the chapter on acids and bases'. It is short, ten minutes, so it cannot cover the whole semester.

text: Listen to a voicemail message from a university advisor.
script: M: Hi, Amara. This is Mr. Brown from the Academic Advising Office, returning your call.
M: You asked about adding a statistics class to your schedule. The good news is that there are still three seats open in the Tuesday and Thursday section at one o'clock.
M: To add the class, you must fill out the add form and bring it to my office by this Friday. After Friday, the seats may be gone.
M: I'm in my office every day from nine to four, and you do not need an appointment. Please bring your student number. See you soon.

stem: Why is Mr. Brown calling Amara?
options: To give her a final grade for statistics
To answer her question about a class
To invite her to a new advising course
To cancel her Tuesday and Thursday class
explanation: Mr. Brown says he is 'returning your call' about adding a statistics class and explains how. No grade or cancellation is mentioned.

stem: What does Amara need to do by Friday?
options: Bring her form to his office
Make an appointment online
Choose a class for Thursday
Pay for the statistics course
explanation: He says 'fill out the add form and bring it to my office by this Friday'. She does not need an appointment, so making one is not required.

text: Listen to an announcement about a computer lab.
script: W: Attention, students. This is a notice from the Information Technology Office.
W: The computer lab in the Library Building will be closed this weekend for new software updates. It will be closed from Friday at six in the evening until Monday at eight in the morning.
W: During this time, students can use the smaller lab on the second floor of the Engineering Building. That lab has twenty computers, and it is open until midnight.
W: Please save your work to the cloud or to a flash drive before Friday evening. Files left on the lab computers may be deleted during the update. Thank you.

stem: What is the announcement mainly about?
options: A weekend closing of the computer lab
The purchase of many new lab computers
A new rule about printing
The opening of a new engineering course
explanation: The speaker says the Library Building lab 'will be closed this weekend' for updates. Computers are not being bought; the software is being updated.

stem: What should students do before Friday evening?
options: Pay a fee for the new software update
Delete all of their old files from home
Visit the Engineering Building lab early
Save their work somewhere safe
explanation: The speaker says 'save your work to the cloud or to a flash drive'. Deleting is what might happen to files left on the computers, so students should avoid it.

text: Listen to an announcement about a student club.
script: M: Hello, everyone. I'm Kwame from the Photography Club, and I have good news.
M: This month we're holding a photo contest called Life on Campus. Anyone can enter, even if you are not in the club.
M: Each person can send in up to three photos, taken on campus. The photos can show people, buildings, nature, or anything you find interesting.
M: The last day to send photos is the twenty-eighth. The winners will get a small prize, and their photos will be shown in the Student Center. For more information, look for our posters or email us.

stem: What is the speaker's main purpose?
options: To sell cameras to members
To announce a campus photo contest
To advertise a photography class
To ask for help at the Student Center
explanation: Kwame says 'we're holding a photo contest called Life on Campus' and describes the rules. He mentions no class, and the Student Center is only where winning photos will be shown.

stem: Who is allowed to enter the contest?
options: Only members of the Photography Club
Only first-year students
Only students who study art
Any student on campus
explanation: Kwame says 'Anyone can enter, even if you are not in the club.' The words 'only members' reverses this, and nothing limits entry by year or subject.

text: Listen to an announcement about parking.
script: W: Good morning. This announcement is for everyone who parks on campus.
W: Starting next Monday, Lot C, behind the sports center, will be closed for two weeks while workers repair the road surface.
W: Students who normally park in Lot C can use Lot F, near the west gate, for free during this time. A shuttle bus will take you from Lot F to the main buildings every ten minutes.
W: Parking passes from Lot C will work in Lot F, so you do not need to buy a new one. If you have questions, please call the Parking Office. Thank you for your cooperation.

stem: Why will Lot C be closed?
options: It is too small for the number of cars
It will be used for a sports event
The road needs repair work
A new building is being built
explanation: The speaker says workers will 'repair the road surface'. The sports center is only the lot's location, not the reason.

stem: What should students who normally use Lot C do?
options: Park in Lot F and use their same pass
Buy a new parking pass for Lot F
Take the shuttle bus from their homes
Park in front of the sports center gym
explanation: The speaker says to use Lot F and adds that 'Parking passes from Lot C will work in Lot F'. A shuttle runs from Lot F, but nothing suggests staying away from campus.

text: Listen to an announcement in an art history class.
script: M: Good morning, class. Before we begin, I want to tell you about a change to next week's schedule.
M: On Wednesday, we will not meet in our usual classroom. Instead, we will visit the City Art Museum, where we will look at the paintings we have studied in the textbook.
M: The museum opens at ten, so please meet me at the front entrance at a quarter to ten. Student tickets are free if you show your card.
M: You will write a short report about one painting, and it is due the following Monday. Bring a notebook, but remember that photographs inside the galleries are not allowed.

stem: What is the professor announcing?
options: A new textbook for the class
The cancellation of Wednesday's class
A class visit to a museum
A free lecture by a painter
explanation: The professor says 'we will visit the City Art Museum' instead of meeting in the classroom. The class is not cancelled, because it simply meets somewhere else.

stem: What must students write after the visit?
options: A report on one painting
A formal letter to the museum director
A list of all the museum galleries
An essay about the textbook
explanation: The professor says 'You will write a short report about one painting'. The textbook paintings are what students see, but the report is about one painting from the visit.

text: Listen to an announcement about a language course.
script: W: Welcome to the Language Center. This is a message for students who signed up for evening English classes.
W: Because of low enrollment, the Tuesday evening class for beginners has been joined with the Thursday evening class. All beginner students will now meet on Thursdays from six to eight.
W: The classroom is the same, Room twelve on the ground floor. Your teacher, Ms. Chen, will also stay the same.
W: If Thursday evening does not work for you, you can ask for a full refund at the office before the end of this week. Please bring your receipt. We apologize for any problem this causes.

stem: What is the main point of the message?
options: A new teacher has replaced Ms. Chen
Two classes became one
The Language Center will move
Evening classes cost more now
explanation: The speaker says the Tuesday class 'has been joined with the Thursday evening class'. The teacher, Ms. Chen, stays the same, and no new price is announced.

stem: What can students do if they cannot attend on Thursday?
options: Join the Tuesday class for advanced students
Study with Ms. Chen at home
Move to Room twelve on Tuesdays
Get their money back at the office
explanation: The speaker says 'you can ask for a full refund at the office' and asks students to bring a receipt. No Tuesday class remains for beginners.

text: Listen to an announcement at an airport shuttle desk.
script: M: Good afternoon, students and visitors. This is an update from the University Airport Shuttle.
M: Our shuttle from the campus to the airport will now leave every hour on the hour, starting at six in the morning. Until now, it left only every two hours.
M: The ride takes about forty minutes, and tickets cost eight dollars each way. You can buy tickets from the driver, but you must have the exact amount, because drivers cannot give change.
M: The pickup point is still the bus circle in front of the Student Center. Please arrive five minutes before departure. Safe travels.

stem: What change does the speaker announce?
options: Tickets are cheaper than before
The shuttle will go to a new airport
The pickup point has moved
The shuttle will leave more often
explanation: The speaker says the shuttle will 'leave every hour' instead of every two hours. The pickup point is 'still' the bus circle, and the price is given but not changed.

stem: What should passengers do when they buy a ticket from the driver?
options: Show a student card
Have the exact money ready
Pay at the Student Center first
Book online one day before
explanation: The speaker says 'you must have the exact amount, because drivers cannot give change'. No student card or booking is mentioned.

text: Listen to an announcement from a campus health center.
script: W: Hello, students. This is the Campus Health Center with an important reminder.
W: Flu season is starting, and we will offer free flu shots next week. The clinic will be open in the Student Center on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday from ten until four.
W: You do not need an appointment. Just bring your student card, and the shot will take only a few minutes.

W: If you have a fever today, please do not come to class or the clinic's event. Stay home, rest, and call our nurse line instead. The number is on our website. Take care of yourselves, and stay healthy.

stem: What is the purpose of the announcement?
options: To offer free flu shots
To ask students to join a nurse team
To explain how to treat a high fever
To close the health center for a week
explanation: The speaker says 'we will offer free flu shots next week' and gives the place and times. A fever is mentioned only as a reason to stay away from the event.

stem: What should a student with a fever today do?
options: Go to the Student Center on Monday
Stay home and call the nurse
Make an appointment at the clinic first
Bring a card to class
explanation: The speaker says 'Stay home, rest, and call our nurse line instead.' The clinic needs no appointment, and the student card is for the flu shot, not a fever.

text: Listen to an announcement about a scholarship.
script: M: Good afternoon. This is the Financial Aid Office with news for first-year students.
M: The deadline for the Founders Scholarship has been extended. You now have until the thirtieth of this month to send in your application, instead of the fifteenth.
M: The scholarship covers half of the tuition for one year. To apply, you need a short essay of about three hundred words, and one letter from a teacher.
M: Applications must be sent through the student portal, not by email. If you need help with your essay, the Writing Center can give you free advice. Good luck to everyone.

stem: What has changed about the scholarship?
options: The amount of the scholarship money
The deadline
The number of required essays
The kind of teacher letter needed
explanation: The speaker says the deadline 'has been extended' to the thirtieth. The scholarship still covers half of the tuition.

stem: How must students send their applications?
options: By email to the office
On paper to the Writing Center
Through the student portal
By asking a teacher to mail it
explanation: The speaker says 'Applications must be sent through the student portal, not by email.' The Writing Center only gives free advice on the essay.

text: Listen to an announcement in a history class.
script: W: Hello, class. I need to tell you about our next assignment before you leave today.
W: Instead of a written test, you will give a short presentation about a famous trade route, such as the Silk Road or the spice routes of the Indian Ocean. Each talk should last five minutes.
W: You may work alone or with one partner. Please send me your topic by email before Friday so that no two students choose the same one.
W: Presentations will begin in two weeks. You can use slides or maps, but you cannot read your talk word for word. I will explain more on Monday.

stem: What is the professor mainly talking about?
options: A new final written test this term
A replacement for a test
A trip to see a trade route
A change in the class meeting schedule
explanation: The professor says 'Instead of a written test, you will give a short presentation'. There is no trip or schedule change.

stem: What must students do before Friday?
options: Practice reading their talk aloud
Give their first presentation
Choose a partner for a debate
Email the professor their topic
explanation: The professor says 'send me your topic by email before Friday'. Presentations start in two weeks, and reading the talk word for word is not allowed.

text: Listen to a voicemail message from a landlord.
script: M: Hello, this is Mr. Garcia, the manager of Riverside Apartments. I'm calling for all tenants in Building B.
M: Next Tuesday, a worker will come to check the heating system in every apartment. The visit will take about twenty minutes, and it will happen between nine and noon.
M: You do not have to be home, but if you are not, I will need to enter with my key. If you prefer to be there, please call me and I will arrange a time.
M: Also, please move any boxes away from the radiators so the worker can reach them. Thank you for your help, and have a pleasant day.

stem: Why is Mr. Garcia calling?
options: To tell tenants of a heating check
To say that the rent will rise soon
To ask tenants to leave the building
To report a problem with the keys
explanation: Mr. Garcia says a worker will 'check the heating system in every apartment'. Keys are mentioned only as a way to enter, and nothing is said about rent.

stem: What should tenants do before the visit?
options: Turn off all the radiators in the morning
Wait for twenty minutes outside
Pay the worker for the check
Clear boxes away from the radiators
explanation: Mr. Garcia asks tenants to 'move any boxes away from the radiators'. Tenants do not have to be home.

text: Listen to an announcement about a student job fair.
script: W: Good morning, everyone. The Career Center is pleased to invite you to this semester's Student Job Fair.
W: It will be held next Thursday in the gym from ten in the morning until three in the afternoon. More than thirty local companies will be there, including restaurants, banks, and a hospital.
W: Many of them are looking for part-time workers, so this is a great chance to find a job that fits your class schedule.
W: Please bring several copies of your résumé and dress neatly. If you do not have a résumé yet, visit the Career Center this week, and a counselor will help you make one. We hope to see you there.

stem: What is the main purpose of the announcement?
options: To advertise a hospital's new clinic
To invite students to a job fair
To offer a class on writing résumés
To list the companies in town
explanation: The speaker says the Career Center 'is pleased to invite you' to the Student Job Fair. Résumé help is a side offer, not the main message.

stem: What should students without a résumé do?
options: Skip the job fair this semester
Ask a company at the gym for help
Go to the Career Center
Write one during the fair
explanation: The speaker says 'visit the Career Center this week, and a counselor will help you make one'. The fair is where the résumé is used, not where it is made.

text: Listen to an announcement in a gym.
script: M: Hello, members of the University Fitness Center. I have a few updates for this month.
M: The swimming pool will be closed from the third to the tenth for cleaning. During that week, you can use our indoor track or the weight room as usual.
M: We are also adding a new yoga class on Wednesday mornings at seven. It is open to everyone, and beginners are welcome. You do not need to bring a mat, because we will provide them.
M: To sign up for yoga, please write your name on the list at the front desk. Space is limited to fifteen people, so sign up early.

stem: What will be unavailable from the third to the tenth?
options: The weight room downstairs
The indoor running track
The yoga room upstairs
The swimming pool
explanation: The speaker says 'The swimming pool will be closed from the third to the tenth'. The track and weight room can be used 'as usual'.

stem: How can someone join the new yoga class?
options: By paying at the pool
By bringing a mat on Wednesday
By calling the instructor
By writing a name on the list
explanation: The speaker says 'write your name on the list at the front desk'. A mat is not needed because the center provides them.

text: Listen to an announcement about a graduation ceremony.
script: W: Good afternoon, seniors. This is the Registrar's Office with details about graduation.
W: The ceremony will take place on Saturday, May tenth, at two o'clock in the Memorial Stadium. Please arrive by one o'clock to line up in alphabetical order.
W: Each graduate will receive four tickets for family and friends. You can pick up your tickets at the Registrar's Office starting next Monday. Extra tickets are not available.
W: Caps and gowns must be returned to the bookstore within two days after the ceremony. Congratulations on your hard work, and we look forward to celebrating with you.

stem: What is the announcement mostly about?
options: Final exams for the seniors
Plans for graduation day
Directions to the stadium by bus
Rules for returning library books
explanation: The speaker gives the date, place, time and tickets for graduation. The only thing returned is caps and gowns, not books.

stem: What can graduates get at the Registrar's Office?
options: Their caps and gowns
Extra tickets for friends
A list of the line order
Four tickets for guests
explanation: The speaker says 'You can pick up your tickets at the Registrar's Office' and each graduate gets four. Caps and gowns are returned to the bookstore, and extra tickets are not available.

text: Listen to an announcement in a physics class.
script: M: Hi, everyone. Please listen carefully because this affects your grade.
M: Professor Alvarez is sick this week, so I'll be teaching your physics class on Wednesday and Friday. My name is Hamza, and I'm the teaching assistant.
M: We will not start the new chapter. Instead, we will review the problems from last week's homework, which many of you found difficult.

The class has become too large
The professor is not well
The midterm has been moved

Take the midterm test early
Begin the next new chapter
Watch a video lecture

text: Listen to an announcement from a bookstore.

The opening of a new store location
To say textbooks are free this week

Buy books for every class on the list
Ask the publisher for a copy of the receipt
Check the list for editions

text: Listen to an announcement about a concert.

A student concert

They pay an extra fee at the door

They are asked to sit near the choir

text: Listen to an announcement in a psychology class.

To teach a lesson about pictures
To announce a quiz about privacy
To ask for study volunteers

A free class on memory skills
Money for each question answered
A copy of the study results

text: Listen to an announcement about a train service.

The Lakeview station will close permanently
A new express train is starting soon
Local trains will replace the express

Use the ticket on Monday only
Ask for a refund
Exchange it at Lakeview station

text: Listen to an announcement in an environmental science class.
script: W: Good afternoon, everyone. I want to tell you about our class project for this semester.

A class project on waste
A test about recycling rules
A talk by a visiting engineer

stem: What must students do before Monday?
options: Choose their groups
Weigh the trash bins
Write a short report
Buy a pair of gloves
explanation: The speaker ends with 'Please choose your groups before Monday.' The report is due Friday, and the professor gives out the gloves.

text: Listen to a voicemail message from a professor.
script: M: Hello, Sofia. This is Professor Lee. I got your email about the essay, and I'm calling to answer your questions.
M: First, yes, you may choose your own topic, but it must be about the industrial age, which we discussed in October.

To change the date of a class
To invite her to a library tour
To answer her essay questions

stem: What must Sofia do if she wants feedback on a draft?
options: Visit the library on Friday
Print it from the database
Send it by next Wednesday
Wait until Thursday morning

text: Listen to an announcement about a cafeteria.
script: W: Hello, diners. This is an update from the Central Cafeteria.

A dessert counter
A second cafeteria
A late-night menu

options: Dinner will start earlier and end later
Dinner will no longer be served
Dinner will be shorter than before
Dinner will cost less on weekdays
explanation: Dinner changes from 'four to nine' to 'five to eight', which is one hour shorter on each end. It is not cancelled and no price change is mentioned.

text: Listen to an announcement for new international students.
script: M: Welcome to the university, and congratulations on your arrival. This is the International Student Office.

To describe a campus tour for tourists

To ask for help at the welcome party

Ask the volunteers in yellow
Wait at the welcome party
Go back to their own rooms for a while
explanation: The speaker says to 'look for volunteers wearing yellow shirts near the main gate'. The advisors are not mentioned as helpers for directions.

text: Listen to an announcement about a lost item.
script: W: Attention, please. This is the Student Center information desk.

To find a backpack owner
To close the information desk early

Describe something in the bag
Bring the water bottle to the desk
Fill out a form online

text: Listen to an announcement in a music class.
script: M: Good morning, everyone. Please take your seats, because I have two quick announcements.
M: First, our class recital will be held on the twelfth of December, instead of the fifth. The concert hall is not free on the fifth, so we had to move it a week later.

The students need more time to practice hard
The professor will be traveling
Some students will be on vacation

Whether they can come to the hall
Which day they prefer to play
What piece they will perform

text: Listen to an announcement about a volunteer program.
script: W: Hi, everyone. My name is Olga, and I'm from the Community Service Office.
W: This Saturday, we are organizing a day of volunteer work at Green Valley Park. We will plant trees, paint benches, and pick up litter. No experience is needed.

Sell tickets to a big park music concert

A packed lunch
Old clothes and water
A tent and a blanket

text: Listen to an announcement about a registration deadline.

The student bill has a new late fee
Registration closes Friday

To collect unpaid bills from students
To print student accounts for the office
To help students in trouble

text: Listen to an announcement in a computer science class.

The wrong day of the week for the lab

text: Listen to an announcement about a bike program.

They are banned for a week
They must return it to the library only

text: Listen to an announcement in an astronomy class.
script: W: Before we start, I'd like to clear up some confusion about Thursday night's observation session.

W: The weather forecast shows clouds moving in after nine, which would make it almost impossible to see Jupiter. So rather than cancel, I'm moving the session up to seven thirty, while the sky should still be clear.

W: That means we'll meet at the observatory a full ninety minutes earlier than the schedule says. If you can't make it at that time, tell me by Wednesday, and I'll arrange a make-up session using the campus telescope.

The telescope needs to be repaired soon
Jupiter will rise much later than expected
Many students asked for an early start time

Email a sketch of the sky by Wednesday
Let the professor know by Wednesday
Go to the observatory on Friday
explanation: The professor says 'tell me by Wednesday, and I'll arrange a make-up session'. The sketch is extra credit for those who attend, so it is not a replacement for the session.

M: If you accept, the monthly cost would be about one third lower than the price of a single room. The contract would be sent to you electronically.

To offer him a different type of room

He will move to the top of the list
He must pay for a single room instead
Someone else may get the room

W: Study rooms and the computer lab on the first floor will stay open, but they may be noisy because of construction. For quiet study, we recommend the reading room in the Law Building.

Asking students to help move all the books
Announcing the closing of the library for summer
Describing new equipment in the computer lab
explanation: The speaker says she wants 'to explain how this will affect you' and then describes the closings and alternatives. The library is not fully closed, since the first floor stays open.

stem: What does the speaker suggest for students who need a quiet place?
options: The first floor study rooms and computer lab
The Law Building reading room
The temporary space in the old gym
The online catalog
explanation: She says 'For quiet study, we recommend the reading room in the Law Building.' The first floor will be noisy, and the old gym holds the books.

text: Listen to an announcement in a business class.
script: M: Good afternoon, everyone. Before you start working on your group presentations, a few points.

M: I have noticed that several groups are planning to present a single, well-known company, such as a sneaker brand or a coffee chain. That is acceptable, but it is hard to say something new about such famous companies.

M: So I'd encourage you to pick a smaller local business, preferably one that you can interview. Real conversations with owners make your analysis much stronger, and they will earn you higher marks for originality.
M: Whichever company you choose, tell me its name by the end of the week, and I'll confirm that no other group has chosen it.

options: Present a famous company in a new way
Choose a small business to interview
Work alone instead of in groups
Study a sneaker brand in great depth
explanation: He encourages groups to 'pick a smaller local business, preferably one that you can interview'. Famous companies are allowed but not recommended, so the sneaker brand is only an example.

stem: Why does the professor want to know each group's choice by the end of the week?
options: To book interviews for all of the groups
To decide which groups earn higher marks
To give the groups time to practice
To avoid two groups repeating a company
explanation: He says he will 'confirm that no other group has chosen it'. Higher marks are linked to originality in interviews, not to the date of choosing.

text: Listen to an announcement about a public transportation pass.

A city plan to build new train stations

They already have a different discount
They will not get the pass this year
They must wait until August twentieth

Dr. Okafor has changed her field of study

Send questions to other departments
Read about banking in advance

text: Listen to a voicemail message from a travel office.

It is farther from the ski slopes

text: Listen to an announcement about a campus safety program.

Send a message to the green-jacket volunteers
Contact the volunteers through their residence hall

Hand them in with the final project
Send them to the people they recorded
Keep them for a possible future project

It may lead to job chances
It is a formal dinner with a dress code
